plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was created (when we received the data).

models.name: shopping_mall_product_reviews
models.description: Customer product reviews with ratings and written feedback. Contains approved reviews from verified purchasers. Reviews are immutable once approved. Separated from moderation queue to maintain proper normalization - each review exists in only one state (approved or pending, never both). Enables independent search, filtering, and management of reviews across articles and customers.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the specific product variant (SKU) being reviewed. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who submitted the review. Links to {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. Must be verified purchaser.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order proving customer purchased this product. Links to {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}. Establishes verified purchase.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who sold this product variant. Links to {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}. Enables seller-specific review tracking.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating from 1-5 representing customer satisfaction. 1=Poor, 2=Fair, 3=Average, 4=Good, 5=Excellent. Required field, must be integer value.

plainFields.name: review_title
plainFields.description: Brief headline summarizing the review. Optional field, maximum 100 characters. Provides quick context for review content.

plainFields.name: review_content
plainFields.description: Main review text with detailed product feedback. Optional field, maximum 1000 characters. Contains customer's specific comments about product quality, usage, condition.

plainFields.name: helpful_count
plainFields.description: Number of customers who found this review helpful. Calculated from helpful votes table. Used for review ranking and relevance.

plainFields.name: unhelpful_count
plainFields.description: Number of customers who found this review not helpful. Calculated from helpful votes table. Used for review quality assessment.

plainFields.name: seller_response
plainFields.description: Optional public response from the seller addressing the review. Maximum 500 characters. Seller can respond to customer feedback.

plainFields.name: seller_response_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller submitted their response to this review. ISO 8601 format with timezone.

plainFields.name: review_status
plainFields.description: Status of the review. Values: 'approved' (visible to customers), 'rejected' (removed due to policy violation), 'deleted' (customer removed), 'archived' (product removed but review preserved). Only approved reviews count toward ratings.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when customer submitted the review. ISO 8601 format. Used for sorting reviews chronologically.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when review was last modified (edited by customer or response added). Updated on every change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when review was deleted by customer or admin. Null if review is not deleted. Enables soft delete and historical tracking.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_moderation_queue
models.description: Pending product reviews awaiting moderation before approval. Contains newly submitted reviews with 'pending_moderation' status. Separate from approved reviews to maintain proper normalization - review exists in moderation queue OR approved reviews, never both. Enables review moderation workflow and audit trail.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant being reviewed. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to customer who submitted the review. Links to {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller. Links to {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating from 1-5 submitted by customer pending approval.

plainFields.name: review_title
plainFields.description: Review title pending moderation. Maximum 100 characters.

plainFields.name: review_content
plainFields.description: Review text pending moderation. Maximum 1000 characters. Will be sanitized and checked for policy violations.

plainFields.name: moderation_reason
plainFields.description: Reason why this review was flagged for moderation. Examples: 'spam_detected', 'external_links', 'profanity', 'policy_violation', 'routine_review'. Helps moderator prioritize.

plainFields.name: moderation_priority
plainFields.description: Priority level for moderation. Values: 'low' (routine review), 'medium' (minor flags), 'high' (policy violations), 'critical' (severe issues). Higher priority reviewed first.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when review was submitted. ISO 8601 format. Used to track moderation SLA (24-hour target).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when moderation record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_moderation_history
models.description: Audit trail recording all review moderation decisions and actions. Captures every approval, rejection, and modification of reviews. Immutable snapshot of moderation workflow. Enables tracking of moderation patterns, compliance auditing, and decision transparency.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_review_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the review being moderated. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews.id} or null if review was rejected and never published.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the admin who made this moderation decision. Links to {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: moderation_action
plainFields.description: Action taken during moderation. Values: 'approved' (made visible to customers), 'rejected' (hidden due to violations), 'flagged_for_review' (needs additional review), 'removed' (deleted after approval), 'edited' (content modified during moderation). Tracks complete decision.

plainFields.name: original_rating
plainFields.description: Star rating from submitted review. Captured for audit trail to track if rating changed.

plainFields.name: original_title
plainFields.description: Original review title as submitted. Captured before any edits.

plainFields.name: original_content
plainFields.description: Original review content as submitted. Captured before any edits or sanitization.

plainFields.name: moderation_notes
plainFields.description: Detailed notes from moderator explaining their decision. Maximum 1000 characters. May reference policy violations, content issues, or special circumstances.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: If action was 'rejected', the specific reason. Values: 'spam', 'profanity', 'harassment', 'misleading', 'external_links', 'policy_violation', 'other'. Helps customer understand why review was rejected.

plainFields.name: can_resubmit
plainFields.description: Whether customer can resubmit a modified version after rejection. False if severe policy violation (prevents repeated violations).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderation decision was recorded. ISO 8601 format. Captures when moderator took action.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes
models.description: Customer votes on whether reviews were helpful. Tracks which customers voted on which reviews to prevent duplicate voting. Separate table enables one-vote-per-customer-per-review constraint. Used to rank reviews by helpfulness and identify valuable feedback.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_review_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the review being voted on. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer voting on review. Links to {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. Prevents same customer voting multiple times.

plainFields.name: vote_type
plainFields.description: Type of vote: 'helpful' (found review useful) or 'unhelpful' (did not find review useful). Determines if vote increments helpful or unhelpful count.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when customer submitted their vote. ISO 8601 format. Records when vote was cast.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_ratings_summary
models.description: Denormalized materialized view aggregating product ratings. Pre-calculates average rating, total review count, and rating distribution for each product. Provides fast access to rating data without expensive aggregation queries. Read-only table updated via batch job.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant these ratings summarize. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}. Aggregates all reviews for this variant.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Calculated average star rating (1-5 scale). Rounded to 1 decimal place. Only includes approved reviews. Used for product ranking and display.

plainFields.name: total_reviews
plainFields.description: Total count of approved reviews for this product. Zero if no reviews exist. Used for confidence indicator.

plainFields.name: rating_1_count
plainFields.description: Count of 1-star reviews. Used for rating distribution display.

plainFields.name: rating_2_count
plainFields.description: Count of 2-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_3_count
plainFields.description: Count of 3-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_4_count
plainFields.description: Count of 4-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_5_count
plainFields.description: Count of 5-star reviews.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this materialized view was last calculated/refreshed. ISO 8601 format. Indicates freshness of aggregated data.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_ratings_summary
models.description: Denormalized materialized view aggregating seller performance ratings. Pre-calculates seller's average rating across all their products, review count, and performance trends. Used for seller ranking, storefront display, and performance monitoring. Read-only table updated via batch job.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller these ratings summarize. Links to {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}. Aggregates all reviews for seller's products.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Calculated average seller rating (1-5 scale). Rounded to 1 decimal place. Aggregates across all seller's products. Used for seller ranking.

plainFields.name: total_reviews
plainFields.description: Total count of reviews across all seller's products. Used for seller credibility indication.

plainFields.name: on_time_delivery_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of orders delivered on or before estimated delivery date. 0-100 scale. Calculated from order fulfillment data.

plainFields.name: return_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of orders returned by customers. 0-100 scale. Indicates product quality satisfaction.

plainFields.name: customer_satisfaction_score
plainFields.description: Composite score combining ratings, return rate, and on-time delivery. 0-100 scale. Used for seller tier calculation and visibility.

plainFields.name: rating_trend_30_days
plainFields.description: Trend of seller rating over last 30 days. Values: 'improving', 'stable', 'declining'. Indicates recent performance direction.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this materialized view was last calculated/refreshed. ISO 8601 format.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_flags
models.description: Flags on reviews indicating content issues or community reports. Tracks customer-reported inappropriate reviews and system-detected violations. Enables review moderation queue management and content policy enforcement.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_review_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the flagged review. Links to {@link shopping_mall_product_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to customer who reported the flag (if user-reported). Links to {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. Null if system-generated flag.

plainFields.name: flag_type
plainFields.description: Category of flag. Values: 'spam' (promotional/irrelevant), 'abusive' (offensive language/harassment), 'misleading' (false claims), 'external_links' (promotional URLs), 'policy_violation' (other violations), 'system_detected' (automated scan). Used for prioritization.

plainFields.name: flag_reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of why review was flagged. Maximum 500 characters. Provides context for moderation team.

plainFields.name: flag_source
plainFields.description: Source of flag. Values: 'customer_report' (customer reported), 'system_scan' (automated detection), 'admin_manual' (admin flagged manually). Indicates trustworthiness.

plainFields.name: flag_status
plainFields.description: Current status of flag. Values: 'open' (awaiting action), 'investigating' (under review), 'resolved' (action taken), 'dismissed' (not a violation). Tracks moderation workflow.

plainFields.name: resolution_notes
plainFields.description: Notes from moderator about how flag was resolved. Maximum 500 characters. Documents decision and rationale.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when flag was created. ISO 8601 format. Indicates when issue was first reported.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when flag was resolved. ISO 8601 format. Null if flag still open.

models.name: shopping_mall_return_requests
models.description: Customer-initiated return requests for delivered orders. Stores the initial return request with customer reason, optional evidence (photos), and desired resolution. This is the first stage of the return lifecycle where customers express intent to return a product.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order being returned. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who initiated the return request. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_line_item_id
foreignFields.description: Specific line item being returned (if partial return). {@link shopping_mall_order_line_items.id}

plainFields.name: return_request_number
plainFields.description: Human-readable return request number in format RR-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX for customer reference

plainFields.name: return_reason
plainFields.description: Customer-selected reason for return: Item not as described, Item arrived defective, Wrong item received, Item arrived damaged, Changed mind, Not needed, Other reason

plainFields.name: additional_details
plainFields.description: Customer's detailed explanation of return reason (up to 500 characters)

plainFields.name: requested_resolution
plainFields.description: Customer's desired outcome: Full refund, Replacement, Store credit, Partial refund

plainFields.name: quantity_to_return
plainFields.description: Number of units customer wants to return (for multi-unit orders)

plainFields.name: evidence_urls
plainFields.description: JSON array of uploaded evidence image URLs (max 3 images) for damaged/defective items

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Return request status: pending, authorized, rejected, dispute_opened, withdrawn. Controls workflow progression.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when return request was initiated by customer

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for return request

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp if return request is withdrawn

models.name: shopping_mall_return_authorizations
models.description: Seller's authorization decision on customer return requests. Records whether seller approves or rejects the return, with reason and timestamp. This is the authorization stage where seller determines if return is eligible.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_request_id
foreignFields.description: Associated return request being authorized. {@link shopping_mall_return_requests.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller making the authorization decision. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: authorization_decision
plainFields.description: Seller's decision: approved, rejected, more_information_requested. Controls next workflow step.

plainFields.name: decision_reason
plainFields.description: Seller's explanation for approval or rejection of return

plainFields.name: requested_information
plainFields.description: If decision is 'more_information_requested', details about what information customer should provide

plainFields.name: information_deadline
plainFields.description: Deadline for customer to provide additional information (typically 7 days from authorization)

plainFields.name: return_shipping_address
plainFields.description: Full return shipping address seller will accept returns to

plainFields.name: prepaid_label_tracking_number
plainFields.description: Tracking number if prepaid return shipping label was provided by seller

plainFields.name: authorized_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller made the authorization decision

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when authorization record was created

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for authorization

models.name: shopping_mall_return_shipments
models.description: Tracks the physical return shipment journey from customer back to seller. Records carrier, tracking number, and shipping status as return moves through logistics. This is the shipment stage of the return lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_request_id
foreignFields.description: Associated return request being shipped. {@link shopping_mall_return_requests.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_authorization_id
foreignFields.description: Associated return authorization approval. {@link shopping_mall_return_authorizations.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer initiating the return shipment. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_shipping_carrier_id
foreignFields.description: Carrier handling the return shipment (optional). {@link shopping_mall_shipping_carriers.id}

plainFields.name: return_tracking_number
plainFields.description: Carrier tracking number for outbound return shipment provided by customer

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Shipping carrier name (FedEx, UPS, DHL, etc.) for the return

plainFields.name: origin_address
plainFields.description: Customer's address from which return is being shipped

plainFields.name: destination_address
plainFields.description: Seller's return receiving address (typically seller's warehouse)

plainFields.name: shipment_status
plainFields.description: Return shipment status: not_shipped, in_transit, received_by_seller, returned_to_customer. Tracks physical journey.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when customer shipped the return (based on carrier pickup)

plainFields.name: received_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller confirmed receipt of return shipment

plainFields.name: expected_receipt_date
plainFields.description: Estimated date seller expects to receive return based on carrier estimate

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when return shipment record was created

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for return shipment

models.name: shopping_mall_return_inspections
models.description: Records seller's inspection of received return item. Documents item condition, whether condition is acceptable for refund, and any deductions (restocking fees, condition issues). This is the inspection stage after return is received.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Return shipment being inspected. {@link shopping_mall_return_shipments.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller performing the inspection. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: inspection_status
plainFields.description: Inspection outcome: pending, approved, rejected, partial_approval. Determines if refund proceeds.

plainFields.name: item_condition_assessment
plainFields.description: Seller's assessment of returned item condition: new, like_new, good, fair, poor, damaged_unsaleable

plainFields.name: condition_details
plainFields.description: Detailed description of item condition, visible wear, damage, missing components, etc.

plainFields.name: sku_verification
plainFields.description: Verification that returned item matches ordered SKU: verified_match, mismatch, unable_to_verify

plainFields.name: all_accessories_present
plainFields.description: Whether all original accessories, documentation, and components are included

plainFields.name: missing_items
plainFields.description: List of missing accessories or components if not all present

plainFields.name: refund_deduction_percentage
plainFields.description: Percentage deduction from refund for condition issues (0, 10, 25, 50, 100 for no refund)

plainFields.name: deduction_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for any refund deduction applied

plainFields.name: inspection_notes
plainFields.description: Seller's detailed inspection notes and findings

plainFields.name: inspection_evidence_urls
plainFields.description: JSON array of photos taken during inspection showing item condition

plainFields.name: inspected_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when inspection was completed

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when inspection record was created

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for inspection

models.name: shopping_mall_return_decisions
models.description: Final decision on return and refund eligibility after inspection. Documents whether return is approved for full/partial/no refund, with calculated refund amount and reasoning. This synthesizes return request through inspection into final decision.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_request_id
foreignFields.description: Original return request being decided upon. {@link shopping_mall_return_requests.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_inspection_id
foreignFields.description: Associated inspection findings (if applicable). {@link shopping_mall_return_inspections.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Original order being returned. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller providing final decision (or admin if escalated). {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: decision_status
plainFields.description: Final decision: approved_full_refund, approved_partial_refund, rejected, disputed, admin_override

plainFields.name: original_order_amount
plainFields.description: Original order total amount in base currency

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: Amount to be refunded to customer (may be less than original due to deductions)

plainFields.name: deductions
plainFields.description: JSON object documenting all deductions: restocking_fee, condition_deduction, shipping_cost_retained, etc.

plainFields.name: decision_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for the decision (why full/partial/no refund)

plainFields.name: appeal_eligible
plainFields.description: Whether customer can appeal this decision (typically true unless fraud detected)

plainFields.name: decided_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when decision was finalized

plainFields.name: decision_made_by
plainFields.description: Who made the decision: seller, admin, system_auto, dispute_resolution

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when decision record was created

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for decision

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_processing
models.description: Tracks refund processing workflow from approval through completion. Records refund payment method, status, and timeline. This is the financial execution stage where refund is actually paid to customer.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_decision_id
foreignFields.description: Associated return decision authorizing the refund. {@link shopping_mall_return_decisions.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Original order being refunded. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer receiving the refund. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller responsible for refund (usually product seller). {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: refund_number
plainFields.description: Unique refund identifier in format REF-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: Amount being refunded to customer in base currency

plainFields.name: refund_method
plainFields.description: Refund destination: original_card, original_account, store_credit, bank_transfer, check

plainFields.name: refund_status
plainFields.description: Refund processing status: pending, initiated, processing, completed, failed, reversed. Controls payment state.

plainFields.name: payment_processor_transaction_id
plainFields.description: Transaction ID from payment processor for the refund (if applicable)

plainFields.name: refund_initiated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when refund processing was initiated

plainFields.name: refund_completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when refund was successfully completed (appeared in customer account)

plainFields.name: expected_arrival_date
plainFields.description: Estimated date refund will appear in customer's account (typically 3-5 business days)

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: If refund failed, reason for failure (invalid payment method, account closed, etc.)

plainFields.name: retry_count
plainFields.description: Number of times refund has been attempted (max 3 retries before escalation)

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when refund record was created

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for refund

models.name: shopping_mall_restocking_inventory
models.description: Records when returned items are restocked into seller's inventory. Tracks whether returned item is marked as new, open-box, or used, and the inventory restoration process. This links returns back to inventory system for stock replenishment.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_inspection_id
foreignFields.description: Associated inspection confirming item acceptable for restocking. {@link shopping_mall_return_inspections.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant (SKU) being restocked. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller whose inventory is being replenished. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_return_request_id
foreignFields.description: Associated return request that triggered restocking. {@link shopping_mall_return_requests.id}

plainFields.name: quantity_restocked
plainFields.description: Number of units being added back to inventory

plainFields.name: restock_condition
plainFields.description: Condition of restocked item: new, open_box, used, refurbished. Determines how it can be sold.

plainFields.name: restock_status
plainFields.description: Restock processing status: pending, approved, failed_no_inventory_slot, completed

plainFields.name: restock_reason
plainFields.description: Why item is being restocked: return_approved, quality_check_passed, inventory_correction

plainFields.name: inventory_movement_id
plainFields.description: Reference to corresponding inventory movement record in inventory system (if synchronized)

plainFields.name: resale_permission
plainFields.description: Whether this item can be resold to other customers (false if item is defective/unsaleable)

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Additional notes about restock condition or handling requirements

plainFields.name: restocked_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when item was added back to inventory

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when restocking record was created

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for restocking

models.name: shopping_mall_disputes
models.description: Core dispute entity representing a customer-seller dispute or complaint. Stores the central dispute record with all metadata but not the detailed evidence, communications, or resolutions (those are in separate tables). This is the primary entity that other dispute-related tables reference.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order involved in this dispute. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who initiated the dispute. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller involved in the dispute. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: dispute_id
plainFields.description: Unique human-readable dispute identifier in format DIS-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS-XXXXXX for easy reference by users.

plainFields.name: dispute_type
plainFields.description: Type of dispute: quality_issue, delivery_issue, seller_communication, payment_issue, other. Categorizes the nature of the complaint.

plainFields.name: reason_description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the dispute reason provided by the customer when initiating the dispute (up to 2000 characters).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current dispute status: open, under_review, pending_resolution, resolved, closed, appealed. Reflects the current stage of dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Dispute priority level: low, medium, high, critical. Used for triage and admin review ordering.

plainFields.name: initiator_type
plainFields.description: Who initiated the dispute: customer, seller, admin, system. Tracks the originating actor.

plainFields.name: assigned_admin_id
plainFields.description: ID of the admin assigned to review/resolve this dispute (optional until assignment).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when dispute was created (ISO 8601 format with timezone).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the dispute record.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when dispute was marked as resolved (null if not yet resolved).

plainFields.name: estimated_resolution_date
plainFields.description: Expected date when dispute should be resolved (based on SLA - typically 5 business days from creation).

models.name: shopping_mall_dispute_evidence
models.description: Stores evidence and supporting documentation provided by dispute parties (customer, seller, witnesses). Each evidence record is immutable once created. Separate from dispute table to prevent nullable fields and ensure evidence integrity.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_dispute_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent dispute this evidence belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_disputes.id}.

plainFields.name: evidence_type
plainFields.description: Type of evidence: photo, message, receipt, tracking, description, document, other. Categorizes the evidence kind.

plainFields.name: submitted_by_type
plainFields.description: Who submitted this evidence: customer, seller, admin, system. Identifies the evidence source.

plainFields.name: submitted_by_id
plainFields.description: ID of the user or system entity that submitted the evidence.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Brief title or description of the evidence (up to 255 characters).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the evidence and its relevance to the dispute (up to 2000 characters).

plainFields.name: file_url
plainFields.description: URL to the evidence file if uploaded (photo, document, etc.). Null if evidence is text-only.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original file name if file was uploaded (up to 255 characters).

plainFields.name: file_size_bytes
plainFields.description: Size of uploaded file in bytes (null if no file uploaded).

plainFields.name: file_mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of uploaded file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf). Null if text-only.

plainFields.name: is_public
plainFields.description: Whether this evidence is visible to all dispute parties or only to admins/submitter. Sensitive evidence may be admin-only.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when evidence was submitted (ISO 8601 format).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp if evidence was removed (null if active). Evidence is not hard-deleted for audit purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_dispute_communications
models.description: Tracks all communications between dispute parties (customer, seller, admin) related to the dispute. Creates audit trail of all messages, responses, and interactions throughout dispute lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_dispute_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent dispute this communication relates to. {@link shopping_mall_disputes.id}.

plainFields.name: message_type
plainFields.description: Type of message: customer_message, seller_response, admin_communication, system_notification, status_update. Categorizes message purpose.

plainFields.name: sender_type
plainFields.description: Type of sender: customer, seller, admin, system. Identifies who sent the message.

plainFields.name: sender_id
plainFields.description: ID of the user or system that sent the message.

plainFields.name: recipient_type
plainFields.description: Who receives this message: customer, seller, admin, all_parties, system. Determines visibility.

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description: Subject line of the message (up to 255 characters).

plainFields.name: message_body
plainFields.description: Full message content (up to 5000 characters). The actual communication text.

plainFields.name: is_internal_note
plainFields.description: Whether this is an internal admin note (only visible to admins) or party-facing communication (visible to relevant parties).

plainFields.name: is_automated
plainFields.description: Whether this is an automated system message (e.g., status update notification) or manually written message.

plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.name: enforcement_status

plainFields.description: User agent string from client device (browser/device information). Helps identify device used for action.

### `shopping_mall_channels`

Core system channels representing different seller communities or market
segments. Channels organize the overall marketplace structure and enable
multiple independent market communities to operate within the platform.
Each channel has its own configuration for commission rates, policies,
and branding.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `channel_code`
  > Unique channel identifier code in format like CHANNEL_PRIMARY,
  > CHANNEL_LUXURY, etc. Used in URLs and system references. Maximum 50
  > characters.
- `channel_name`
  > Display name for the channel shown to customers and sellers. Example:
  > 'Primary Marketplace', 'Premium Store', 'Local Sellers'. Maximum 100
  > characters.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the channel's purpose and positioning. Helps
  > sellers understand which channel suits their business. Maximum 1000
  > characters.
- `base_commission_rate`
  > Default commission percentage (0-100) charged to sellers in this channel.
  > Example: 10.5 means 10.5% commission. Specific product categories can
  > override this.
- `min_order_value`
  > Minimum order value in platform currency required for orders in this
  > channel. Prevents very small orders. Example: 100.00
- `is_active`
  > Whether this channel is currently active and accepting new sellers and
  > orders. Inactive channels may have read-only access.
- `display_order`
  > Sort order for displaying channels in user interfaces. Lower numbers
  > appear first. Used for UI ordering, not business logic.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this channel was created in the system. ISO 8601 format
  > with timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this channel was last updated. Updated whenever any
  > channel field changes. ISO 8601 format with timezone.

### `shopping_mall_sections`

Organizational sections within channels that group related product
categories. Sections provide a second-level organization hierarchy
between channels and specific product categories. Enables structured
navigation for customers browsing products. Example sections:
Electronics, Clothing, Home & Garden.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_channel_id`
  > Reference to the parent channel this section belongs to. {@link
  > shopping_mall_channels.id}
- `section_code`
  > Unique section identifier code within a channel. Format:
  > SECTION_ELECTRONICS, SECTION_FASHION. Maximum 50 characters.
- `section_name`
  > Display name for the section shown in navigation and category browsing.
  > Example: 'Electronics & Gadgets'. Maximum 100 characters.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the section's scope and types of products
  > included. Helps customers understand what products are in this section.
  > Maximum 500 characters.
- `section_image_url`
  > URL to an image/icon representing this section for visual display in
  > category navigation. Optional visual identifier.
- `display_order`
  > Sort order for displaying sections within parent channel. Lower numbers
  > appear first in UI navigation.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this section is currently active. Inactive sections are hidden
  > from customer view but preserved for historical data.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this section was created. ISO 8601 format with timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this section was last updated. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.

### `shopping_mall_categories`

Product categories that organize the product catalog into hierarchical
browsing structure. Categories enable customers to navigate and discover
products. Categories can be nested in a tree structure where each
category may have a parent category. Examples: Smartphones, Laptops,
Clothing, Shoes, Accessories. Used for both customer browsing and seller
product organization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_category_id`
  > Reference to parent category in hierarchical structure for nested
  > categories. Null if this is a top-level category. {@link
  > shopping_mall_categories.id}
- `category_code`
  > Unique category identifier code used internally. Format: CAT_ELECTRONICS,
  > CAT_SMARTPHONES, etc. Maximum 50 characters.
- `category_name`
  > Display name for the category shown in navigation and product listings.
  > Example: 'Smartphones', 'Laptop Computers'. Maximum 100 characters.
- `category_slug`
  > URL-friendly slug for SEO and navigation URLs. Lowercase alphanumeric
  > with hyphens. Example: 'smartphones', 'laptop-computers'. Maximum 100
  > characters.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of products in this category. Displayed on category
  > landing page. Maximum 1000 characters.
- `category_image_url`
  > URL to an image/icon representing this category for visual display in
  > navigation and category pages.
- `display_order`
  > Sort order for displaying categories at same hierarchy level. Lower
  > numbers appear first in navigation.
- `product_count`
  > Denormalized count of active products in this category (includes products
  > in subcategories). Updated when products are added/removed from category.
  > Used for display efficiency.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this category is currently visible to customers. Inactive
  > categories are hidden but preserved for historical data and existing
  > product references.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this category was created. ISO 8601 format with timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this category was last updated. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.

### `shopping_mall_category_attributes`

Configurable attributes that products in a specific category can have.
Attributes define the possible variants (colors, sizes, materials, etc.)
that products in a category can use. Enables structured product variant
management and customer filtering. Example: In Clothing category,
attributes might be Color, Size, Material, Style.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_category_id`
  > Reference to the category these attributes are available for. {@link
  > shopping_mall_categories.id}
- `attribute_code`
  > Unique identifier for this attribute within the category. Format:
  > ATTR_COLOR, ATTR_SIZE, ATTR_MATERIAL. Maximum 50 characters.
- `attribute_name`
  > Display name for the attribute. Example: 'Color', 'Size', 'Material'.
  > Maximum 100 characters.
- `attribute_type`
  > Data type of attribute values: 'text' (free text), 'number' (numeric
  > values), 'selection' (predefined options from attribute_values),
  > 'boolean' (true/false toggle). Determines how attribute values are
  > managed and displayed.
- `attribute_values`
  > JSON array of predefined values for selection-type attributes. Example:
  > ["Red", "Blue", "Green"] for color. Null for text/number types. Stored as
  > JSON string.
- `is_required_for_variant`
  > Whether products in this category MUST specify a value for this attribute
  > when creating variants. Mandatory attributes for variant definition.
- `is_filterable`
  > Whether customers can filter products by this attribute in category view.
  > Affects customer-facing filtering options.
- `display_order`
  > Sort order for displaying attributes in variant selector and product
  > forms. Lower numbers appear first.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this attribute was created. ISO 8601 format with timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this attribute was last updated. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.

### `shopping_mall_configurations`

Global platform configuration settings for feature toggles, system
behavior, and operational policies. Single-purpose configuration table
storing key-value pairs that control platform-wide behavior. Examples:
enable/disable review system, enable/disable wishlist feature, maximum
cart items, etc.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `config_key`
  > Unique configuration key identifier. Format: 'feature_reviews_enabled',
  > 'feature_wishlist_enabled', 'max_cart_items',
  > 'default_order_timeout_minutes'. Maximum 100 characters. Used as primary
  > identifier for lookups.
- `config_value`
  > Configuration value as string. Interpretations: 'true'/'false' for
  > boolean flags, numeric strings for numbers, JSON for complex objects.
  > Stored as text for flexibility. Maximum 5000 characters.
- `config_type`
  > Data type indicator: 'boolean', 'integer', 'decimal', 'string', 'json'.
  > Helps with value interpretation and validation.
- `description`
  > Human-readable description of this configuration's purpose and expected
  > values. Helps admins understand what each setting controls. Maximum 500
  > characters.
- `is_editable`
  > Whether admins can modify this configuration from the admin panel. Some
  > system-critical configs may be read-only. Controls admin UI visibility.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration was created. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration was last updated. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.

### `shopping_mall_system_settings`

System-wide operational settings for business rules, policies, and
limits. Stores global business settings like minimum order values,
maximum product price, commission structures, default timeouts, and
policy parameters. Unlike configurations which are feature toggles,
settings are business rule values.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `setting_name`
  > Identifier for this setting. Format: 'minimum_order_value',
  > 'maximum_product_price', 'default_commission_rate',
  > 'payment_timeout_minutes', 'order_cancellation_window_hours'. Maximum 100
  > characters.
- `setting_value`
  > Value for this setting as string. Numeric settings stored as numeric
  > strings, currency amounts include decimal point. Maximum 1000 characters.
- `setting_unit`
  > Unit of measurement if applicable. Examples: 'currency', 'minutes',
  > 'hours', 'days', 'percentage', 'units'. Helps interpret numeric values.
  > Maximum 50 characters.
- `description`
  > Explanation of what this setting controls and why it matters. Helps
  > admins understand business impact. Maximum 500 characters.
- `min_value`
  > Minimum allowed value for this setting if numeric. Used for validation
  > when setting is updated. Null for non-numeric settings.
- `max_value`
  > Maximum allowed value for this setting if numeric. Used for validation
  > when setting is updated. Null for non-numeric settings.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this setting was created. ISO 8601 format with timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this setting was last updated. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.

### `shopping_mall_supported_countries`

Registry of countries supported by the platform for shipping, tax, and
regulatory purposes. Defines which countries are available for customer
addresses, seller registration, and shipping destinations. Each country
entry includes tax rates, shipping info, and operational flags.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `country_code`
  > ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US', 'GB', 'IN', 'JP'). Used for
  > all country references throughout the system. Exactly 2 uppercase
  > letters.
- `country_name`
  > Full country name as displayed to users (e.g., 'United States', 'United
  > Kingdom', 'India'). Maximum 100 characters.
- `currency_code`
  > ISO 4217 currency code for this country (e.g., 'USD', 'GBP', 'INR'). Used
  > for pricing and financial transactions. Exactly 3 uppercase letters.
- `tax_rate`
  > Default VAT/sales tax rate as percentage (0-100). Example: 15.5 for 15.5%
  > tax. Applied to orders shipping to this country unless category-specific
  > rate exists.
- `postal_code_format`
  > Regular expression pattern for validating postal codes in this country.
  > Example: '^[0-9]{5}(-[0-9]{4})?$' for US zip codes. Used in address
  > validation.
- `is_shipping_available`
  > Whether the platform can ship orders to this country. Used to determine
  > available shipping destinations for customers.
- `is_seller_registration_allowed`
  > Whether sellers can register and operate from this country. May be false
  > for countries with regulatory restrictions.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this country is currently active on the platform. Inactive
  > countries are hidden from selection but historical data is preserved.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this country was added to the system. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this country configuration was last updated. ISO 8601
  > format with timezone.

### `shopping_mall_shipping_carriers`

Shipping carriers available on the platform for order fulfillment.
Registry of carrier integrations including courier services, postal
services, and logistics providers. Stores carrier information, API
endpoints, tracking URL formats, and operational details for carrier
integration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `carrier_code`
  > Unique identifier for this carrier used in system references. Format:
  > 'CARRIER_FEDEX', 'CARRIER_UPS', 'CARRIER_DHL'. Maximum 50 characters.
  > Used for internal references, not display.
- `carrier_name`
  > Display name of the shipping carrier shown to customers and sellers.
  > Example: 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'DHL Express'. Maximum 100 characters.
- `api_endpoint`
  > API endpoint URL for carrier tracking and rate queries. Used by system to
  > integrate with carrier systems. Example: 'https://api.fedex.com/v1/'. May
  > be null for manual carriers.
- `api_key`
  > Encrypted API key or credentials for carrier API authentication. Stored
  > encrypted in database. Decrypted only when needed for API calls. Null if
  > no API integration.
- `tracking_url_format`
  > URL template for customer tracking pages. Format:
  > 'https://tracking.fedex.com/tracking?tracknumbers={TRACKING_NUMBER}'.
  > {TRACKING_NUMBER} is placeholder for actual tracking number.
- `supported_countries_json`
  > JSON array of ISO country codes this carrier operates in. Example:
  > '["US", "CA", "MX"]'. Used to filter available carriers by destination.
- `service_types`
  > JSON array of service types offered (Standard, Express, Overnight, etc.).
  > Format: '["Standard", "Express", "Overnight"]'. Used for service
  > selection during shipping.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this carrier is currently available for shipping. Inactive
  > carriers are hidden from seller selections.
- `is_api_integrated`
  > Whether carrier has active API integration for tracking and rate quotes.
  > False means manual tracking number entry required.
- `sync_interval_minutes`
  > Frequency (in minutes) to poll carrier API for tracking updates. Example:
  > 120 = check every 2 hours. Null or 0 means no automatic syncing.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this carrier was added to the system. ISO 8601 format with
  > timezone.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this carrier configuration was last updated. ISO 8601
  > format with timezone.

### `shopping_mall_customers`

Core customer entity representing end-user shoppers. Stores essential
customer account information including authentication credentials, email
verification status, and account lifecycle management. Customers can
browse products, manage shopping carts, place orders, and leave product
reviews.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Customer's unique email address used for account login and communication.
  > RFC 5322 format validated. Serves as the primary authentication
  > identifier.
- `password_hash`
  > Securely hashed customer password using bcrypt with minimum 10 salt
  > rounds. Never stored in plain text. Used for login authentication.
- `first_name`
  > Customer's first name (1-100 characters). Used for personalization in
  > communications and order confirmations.
- `last_name`
  > Customer's last name (1-100 characters). Used for personalization in
  > communications and order confirmations.
- `phone_number`
  > Customer's phone number in international or local format. Optional
  > contact method for delivery and customer service purposes.
- `email_verified`
  > Flag indicating whether the customer's email address has been verified.
  > Required to be true before customer can place orders. Email verification
  > prevents unauthorized account creation.
- `account_status`
  > Current customer account status: 'active', 'email_unverified',
  > 'suspended', or 'deactivated'. Determines account access level and order
  > placement eligibility.
- `failed_login_attempts`
  > Count of consecutive failed login attempts. Used for security lockout
  > mechanism. Resets to 0 on successful login. Triggers 15-minute lockout
  > after 5 failures.
- `locked_until`
  > Timestamp indicating when account lockout expires after excessive failed
  > login attempts. Null if account is not currently locked. Used to enforce
  > 15-minute security lockout period.
- `created_at`
  > Account creation timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when the customer
  > registered on the platform.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last account modification (profile update, password change,
  > etc.). Updated whenever customer information is modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates customer account has been
  > deactivated. Null for active accounts. Enables account recovery and audit
  > trail maintenance.

### `shopping_mall_customer_sessions`

Authentication sessions for customers. One session per active
device/browser. Records connection context (IP, URL, referrer) for
security tracking and fraud detection. Session expires after 30 days of
inactivity. Enables stateless authentication via JWT tokens while
maintaining optional server-side session records.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`
  > Foreign key reference to customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
  > Links session to the authenticated customer.
- `ip`
  > IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for security
  > tracking, anomaly detection, and fraud prevention.
- `href`
  > Connection URL (HTTP referrer) indicating the page or service from which
  > authentication occurred. Stored for security audit and access pattern
  > analysis.
- `referrer`
  > HTTP referrer header value indicating the source page that initiated the
  > session. Used for tracking where customers came from during
  > authentication.
- `created_at`
  > Session creation timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when authentication
  > session was established.
- `expired_at`
  > Session expiration timestamp indicating when the session ended (either
  > due to timeout, logout, or explicit termination). Null for active
  > sessions. Sessions default to 30-day expiration.

### `shopping_mall_customer_addresses`

Customer delivery and billing addresses. Customers can save multiple
addresses (maximum 10) for convenient checkout. Each address includes
recipient name, complete address details, and delivery/billing
designation. Addresses are profile-related data essential for order
fulfillment and customer convenience.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`
  > Foreign key reference to customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
  > Associates address with the customer account.
- `label`
  > User-friendly address label (e.g., 'Home', 'Work', 'Apartment'). Max 50
  > characters. Helps customer identify which address to use during checkout.
- `recipient_name`
  > Full name of the person to receive the delivery. 2-100 characters. Used
  > on shipping labels and delivery confirmation.
- `street_address_line_1`
  > Primary street address line. 5-200 characters. Includes street number,
  > name, and building/unit details as needed.
- `street_address_line_2`
  > Secondary address line for apartment, suite, or additional location
  > details. Optional. Max 200 characters.
- `city`
  > City or municipality name. 2-100 characters. Validated against known
  > cities in the selected country.
- `state_province`
  > State, province, or regional subdivision code/name. 2-50 characters.
  > Format validated per country requirements.
- `postal_code`
  > Postal/ZIP code. Format varies by country (5-20 characters). Validated
  > against country's postal system requirements for accurate delivery.
- `country_code`
  > ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US', 'GB', 'JP'). Determines tax
  > jurisdiction, shipping options, and address format validation rules.
- `phone_number`
  > Contact phone number for delivery. Validated international or local
  > format. Used by carrier for delivery coordination and customer contact.
- `is_default_shipping`
  > Flag indicating this is the customer's default shipping address. Used to
  > pre-populate checkout shipping field. Only one address per customer can
  > have this set to true.
- `is_default_billing`
  > Flag indicating this is the customer's default billing address. Used to
  > pre-populate checkout billing field. Only one address per customer can
  > have this set to true.
- `address_type`
  > Address type classification: 'shipping', 'billing', or 'both'. Determines
  > whether address is used for delivery, payment, or both purposes.
- `is_verified`
  > Flag indicating address has been validated against address verification
  > service. Verified addresses are more reliable for delivery success.
- `created_at`
  > Address creation timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when customer saved
  > this address.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last address modification. Updated when customer edits
  > address details or changes default designation.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates address has been deleted by
  > customer. Null for active addresses. Preserves historical order
  > references.

### `shopping_mall_sellers`

Core seller entity representing merchants/vendors operating on the
platform. Stores seller business identity, authentication credentials,
verification status, and account lifecycle. Sellers list products, manage
inventory, fulfill orders, and receive payments. Must complete
verification before selling.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Seller's business email address used for authentication and official
  > communications. RFC 5322 format validated. Unique across all seller
  > accounts.
- `password_hash`
  > Securely hashed seller password using bcrypt with minimum 10 salt rounds.
  > Never stored in plain text. Used for seller dashboard login
  > authentication.
- `business_name`
  > Seller's legal business name (2-200 characters). Used for business
  > identification and displayed to customers on seller profile and product
  > listings.
- `business_registration_number`
  > Official business registration/license number from relevant government
  > authority. Used for seller verification and compliance purposes. Format
  > varies by jurisdiction.
- `tax_identification_number`
  > Tax ID, VAT number, or equivalent tax identifier. Required for commission
  > calculation and regulatory compliance. Format varies by country.
- `primary_contact_name`
  > Name of primary contact person for the seller business. Used for
  > verification and communication purposes.
- `primary_contact_phone`
  > Primary contact phone number in valid international or local format. Used
  > for seller verification and urgent business communications.
- `business_address`
  > Complete business address matching registration documents. 5-200
  > characters. Used for seller verification and official correspondence.
- `correspondence_address`
  > Official correspondence address for legal communications. May differ from
  > business address. Used for formal notices and regulatory correspondence.
- `business_description`
  > Description of seller's business and products (50-500 characters).
  > Displayed on seller profile to help customers understand the business.
- `store_name`
  > Store/brand name for display (2-100 characters). Shown to customers on
  > product listings and seller profile. May differ from legal business name.
- `verification_status`
  > Seller verification lifecycle state: 'pending_email_verification',
  > 'pending_approval', 'active', 'verification_rejected',
  > 'permanently_banned'. Controls seller dashboard access and product
  > listing ability.
- `account_status`
  > Current account status: 'active', 'suspended', 'deactivated',
  > 'terminated'. Determines if seller can list products and fulfill orders.
- `failed_login_attempts`
  > Count of consecutive failed login attempts. Resets to 0 on successful
  > login. Triggers 15-minute lockout after 5 failures for security.
- `locked_until`
  > Timestamp when login lockout expires after excessive failures. Null if
  > account not locked. Used to enforce 15-minute security lockout.
- `created_at`
  > Account creation timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when seller applied
  > to the platform.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last account modification (profile update, status change,
  > verification, etc.).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates seller account has been
  > deactivated or terminated. Null for active accounts. Preserves seller
  > history and order records.

### `shopping_mall_seller_sessions`

Authentication sessions for sellers. One session per active
device/browser. Records connection context (IP, URL, referrer) for
security monitoring. Sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity. Enables
secure seller dashboard access while maintaining audit trail of login
activity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Foreign key reference to seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers). Links
  > session to the authenticated seller.
- `ip`
  > IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for seller security
  > tracking and suspicious activity detection.
- `href`
  > Connection URL indicating the seller dashboard or service endpoint where
  > authentication occurred. Stored for security audit.
- `referrer`
  > HTTP referrer header value indicating source page for the session. Used
  > for tracking seller access patterns.
- `created_at`
  > Session creation timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when seller
  > authenticated and session was established.
- `expired_at`
  > Session expiration timestamp. When set, indicates session has ended
  > (logout or timeout). Null for active sessions. Default 30-day expiration.

### `shopping_mall_seller_profiles`

Extended seller profile information including store branding, policies,
and business metadata. Stores seller customization options like logo,
banner images, return policy, shipping policy, and business hours.
Enables sellers to personalize their storefront and communicate their
policies to customers.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Foreign key reference to seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
  > Associates profile with the seller account. 1:1 relationship.
- `store_url_slug`
  > URL-friendly identifier for seller's store (alphanumeric with hyphens,
  > max 50 characters). Used to create seller storefront URL:
  > store.com/seller/{slug}. Must be unique.
- `store_logo_url`
  > URL to seller's store logo image for display on storefront. Image should
  > be 2MB max, JPEG or PNG format with minimum 200x200 pixels resolution.
- `store_banner_url`
  > URL to seller's store banner image displayed at top of storefront. Image
  > should be 5MB max, JPEG or PNG format, recommended dimensions 1200x300
  > pixels.
- `store_description`
  > Seller's store description for public display (max 500 characters). Shown
  > on seller profile to help customers understand the business.
- `return_policy`
  > Seller's return and refund policy text (max 2000 characters). Displayed
  > to customers during checkout and on seller profile. Communicates return
  > window and conditions.
- `shipping_policy`
  > Seller's shipping policy and carrier information (max 2000 characters).
  > Displayed to customers explaining shipping methods, costs, and delivery
  > timeframes.
- `cancellation_policy`
  > Seller's order cancellation policy (max 2000 characters). Explains
  > conditions under which orders can be cancelled and any associated fees or
  > restrictions.
- `contact_email`
  > Seller's public contact email for customer inquiries. May differ from
  > account email. Used for customer communications through the platform.
- `contact_phone`
  > Seller's public contact phone number for customer support. Used when
  > customers need to reach seller directly for urgent issues.
- `business_hours`
  > Seller's customer service business hours (formatted text, max 500
  > characters). Helps customers understand when seller is available for
  > support.
- `website_url`
  > Link to seller's external business website if they have one. Provides
  > additional information about the seller's operations.
- `social_media_links`
  > JSON-formatted social media profile links (e.g., Facebook, Instagram,
  > Twitter). Enables customers to follow and verify seller's presence.
- `created_at`
  > Profile creation timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when seller profile
  > was first created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last profile modification. Updated whenever seller updates
  > policies, images, or business information.

### `shopping_mall_seller_verification_documents`

Documents submitted by sellers for identity and business verification
during onboarding. Stores references to uploaded documentation (business
license, tax certificates, ID proofs, address verification). Enables
platform to verify seller legitimacy and comply with regulatory
requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Foreign key reference to seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
  > Associates verification documents with the seller account.
- `document_type`
  > Type of verification document submitted: 'business_license',
  > 'tax_certificate', 'identity_proof', 'address_verification',
  > 'bank_verification'. Determines what the document proves.
- `document_url`
  > URL to the uploaded document file. Image or PDF format (JPEG, PNG, PDF).
  > Maximum 10MB. Stored in secure cloud storage with access control.
- `document_name`
  > Original filename or descriptive name of the document (max 200
  > characters). Helps identify which specific document this is.
- `issuing_country`
  > ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code indicating where the document was issued.
  > Used for validation rules and compliance checking.
- `document_number`
  > Official document number (e.g., business registration number, license
  > number, passport number, tax ID). Used for verification and
  > cross-checking.
- `issue_date`
  > Date when the document was issued. Used to verify document is not expired
  > or suspiciously recent.
- `expiration_date`
  > Document expiration date if applicable. Null if document has no
  > expiration. Used to verify document is still valid.
- `verification_status`
  > Verification status of this document: 'pending_review', 'approved',
  > 'rejected'. Indicates whether admin has reviewed and validated the
  > document.
- `verification_notes`
  > Admin notes regarding verification (max 1000 characters). Explains reason
  > for approval/rejection or requests for specific clarifications.
- `verified_by_admin_id`
  > Admin user ID who reviewed and verified the document. Null if not yet
  > verified. Used for audit trail of verification decisions.
- `verified_at`
  > Timestamp when document was verified by admin. Null if pending
  > verification. Used to track verification workflow timing.
- `created_at`
  > Document upload timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when seller submitted
  > the document.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last modification (status change, notes update, etc.).

### `shopping_mall_admins`

Platform administrator accounts with system-wide access and control
capabilities. Administrators manage users, moderate content, handle
disputes, process refunds, and oversee platform operations. Require
strong authentication with multi-factor authentication support and
comprehensive audit logging.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Admin's unique email address used for authentication and administrative
  > notifications. RFC 5322 format validated. Must be unique across all admin
  > accounts.
- `password_hash`
  > Securely hashed admin password using bcrypt with minimum 10 salt rounds.
  > Never stored in plain text. Used for admin dashboard login
  > authentication.
- `full_name`
  > Admin's full name (2-100 characters). Used for identification in audit
  > logs and admin interface.
- `admin_level`
  > Admin permission level: 'super_admin', 'operations_admin',
  > 'content_admin', 'financial_admin', 'support_admin'. Determines feature
  > access and operational scope.
- `department`
  > Admin's department or team assignment (max 100 characters). Used for
  > organizational tracking and access control scoping.
- `is_mfa_enabled`
  > Flag indicating whether multi-factor authentication is enabled for this
  > admin. Required for enhanced security. Super admins must have MFA
  > enabled.
- `mfa_method`
  > MFA method preference: 'email_otp', 'authenticator_app', or null if MFA
  > not enabled. Admin can authenticate via selected method.
- `mfa_secret`
  > Encrypted MFA secret key for TOTP authenticator app (if using
  > authenticator). Never displayed to admin. Used for OTP code generation.
- `account_status`
  > Current account status: 'active', 'inactive', 'suspended', 'deactivated'.
  > Determines if admin can access the platform.
- `failed_login_attempts`
  > Count of consecutive failed login attempts. Resets to 0 on successful
  > login. Triggers 15-minute lockout after 5 failures for security.
- `locked_until`
  > Timestamp when login lockout expires. Null if account not locked. Used to
  > enforce 15-minute security lockout for excessive failures.
- `last_login_at`
  > Timestamp of most recent successful admin login. Used for security
  > monitoring and activity tracking. Null if admin never logged in.
- `last_login_ip`
  > IP address from the most recent login. Used for suspicious activity
  > detection and security investigations.
- `created_at`
  > Admin account creation timestamp in UTC timezone. Records when the admin
  > account was first created by existing admin.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last account modification (role change, MFA setup, status
  > update, etc.).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates admin account has been
  > deactivated. Null for active accounts. Preserves admin action audit
  > trail.

Authentication sessions for administrators. Records admin login sessions

Properties as follows:

Role definitions for admin access control and permission management.

access control for fine-grained permission management and organizational
structure.

Properties as follows:

  > Human-friendly permission display name (max 100 characters). Shown in

  > Permission description explaining what action/resource it controls (max

- `category`
  > Permission category for organization: 'users', 'sellers', 'products',

  > grouping related permissions.

  > Risk level of this permission: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'critical'.

  > 'support_admin', 'operations_admin', 'super_admin'. Limits who can
  > perform the action.

- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last permission modification.
